question.text: Which of the following is DEEMED an Accredited Investor under SEBI's framework, and thus not required to obtain a separate Accreditation Certificate?

answer.text: A retail investor with net worth of INR 3 crore
A private limited company with turnover of INR 30 crore
A Category I Foreign Portfolio Investor (FPI), Sovereign Wealth Funds, multilateral agencies, and QIBs as defined under ICDR Regulations
Any Hindu Undivided Family irrespective of income

explanation.text: The Logic: Per SEBI's AI Framework, the following are DEEMED AIs without needing accreditation: Central/State Governments, developmental agencies under them, Funds set up by Central/State Governments, QIBs as per ICDR Regulations, Category I FPIs, Sovereign Wealth Funds, multilateral agencies, and other entities specified by SEBI. The Trap: Option A doesn't meet even the individual minimum. Option B fails body-corporate net-worth test. Option D — HUFs must separately qualify under the income/net-worth test. Cross-Exam Context: XIX-C tests the QIB-vs-Cat-I-FPI-vs-SWF deemed list. XIX-A/B treat this as ancillary. Manager's Pro-Tip: Manager tip: When onboarding a Category I FPI, document the SEBI FPI registration certificate as evidence of 'deemed AI' status — you do NOT need a separate Accreditation Certificate from a KRA-subsidiary accreditation agency. Saves 4-6 weeks in onboarding.
